Align reads to the genome using Rsubread

Source: R/align.R
HORIZON_run_align.Rd

Wraps align for splice-aware RNA-seq alignment against a pre-built Rsubread index. By default, uses the trimmed FASTQ files produced by HORIZON_run_qc_trim. Raw FASTQs from the sample sheet can be used instead by setting use_trimmed = FALSE.

Usage

HORIZON_run_align(
  sample_sheet,
  sample_id,
  index,
  use_trimmed = TRUE,
  threads = 4,
  max_mismatches = 3,
  ...
)

Arguments

sample_sheet

Validated sample sheet data.frame from HORIZON_validate_sample_sheet.

sample_id

Character. Sample ID to process.

index

Character. Path to the Rsubread index basename as passed to HORIZON_build_index.

use_trimmed

Logical. Use trimmed FASTQs from the qc/ subfolder (output of HORIZON_run_qc_trim). Default TRUE. Set to FALSE to align the raw FASTQs listed in the sample sheet.

threads

Integer. Number of alignment threads. Default 4.

max_mismatches

Integer. Maximum mismatches allowed per read. Default 3.

...

Additional arguments passed to align (e.g., minFragLength, maxFragLength, unique, nBestLocations).

Value

Character. Path to the output BAM file, invisibly.

Details

Output BAM is written to <output_dir>/<sample_id>/aligned/. The BAM is unsorted at this stage; pass it to HORIZON_sort_index_bam before counting.

RAM note: Rsubread's RAM usage during alignment is largely determined by the index size. Using a split index (index_split = TRUE in HORIZON_build_index) substantially reduces peak RAM. Thread count has a modest additional effect.
